theorem three_site_hopf_capacity : ∃ r₀ w : ℝ, ∃ g : ℝ → ℂ,
    0<r₀ ∧ 0<w ∧ ContDiffAt ℝ ⊤ g r₀ ∧ g r₀=Complex.I*(w:ℂ) ∧
    HasDerivAt (fun s => (g s).re) (deriv g r₀).re r₀ ∧ (deriv g r₀).re<0 ∧
    (∀ᶠ s in 𝓝 r₀, ∃ v : Fin 9 → ℂ, v ≠ 0 ∧ (complexSource s).mulVec v=g s • v) ∧
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0<ε → ∃ (r T : ℝ) (φ : ℝ → State),
      0<r ∧ 0<T ∧ (∀ i, 0<witnessRates r i) ∧
      |r-r₀|<ε ∧ |T-2*Real.pi/w|<ε ∧ Function.Periodic φ T ∧
      (∀ s, HasDerivAt φ (field (witnessRates r) (φ s)) s) ∧
      (∀ s i, 0<φ s i) ∧ (∀ s, ‖φ s-witnessState‖<ε) ∧
      (∀ s, totalE (φ s)=totalE witnessState ∧ totalF (φ s)=totalF witnessState ∧
        totalS (φ s)=totalS witnessState) ∧ ∃ s, φ s ≠ φ 0

    (v1 v2 v3 w1 w2 w3 b2 b3 u2 u3 a1 a2 a3 h1 h2 h3 : ℝ) :

      + 2 * (a2 - h2 - w2) + 3 * (a3 - h3 - w3)
      = v1 + v2 + v3 - w1 - w2 - w3

manuscript_formal_scope: The 31-page published manuscript distinguishes the attracting witness A from the earlier subcritical witness H. The hypothesis-free Lean theorem ThreeSitePhosphorylation.three_site_hopf_capacity proves a transverse source eigenvalue branch and arbitrarily small positive nonconstant periodic solutions of the literal three-site mass-action system in a fixed compatibility class. Its strict saved receipt covers all 52 unchanged modules and a standard-axiom elaborated interface. It asserts neither least period nor stability; the sign of the first Lyapunov coefficient, attraction for witness A and extension to every n >= 3 remain conventional arguments with interval certificates. Two Mathlib-only companion modules support the phosphorylation-balance identity and positivity under relaxation; their wider inventory algebra is preserved as source, not promoted to additional manuscript claims. Finite-amplitude orbit certificates use outward-rounded binary64 arithmetic; exact Hopf certificates and plots have distinct evidence roles. Neither global basins nor connection of the two isolated certified orbits to the Hopf branch is established. Ongoing stronger formalization in the source research task is not part of this frozen publication snapshot.
